summary: AuthnContext (ACR) mismatch prevents SSO access to internal Telemetry Portal
description:
Issue summary: Users intermittently receive '403 Forbidden - insufficient auth context' when accessing the internal Telemetry Portal (telemetry.redwood.internal) after SSO redirection.
Impact: ~15% of engineers and platform SREs report inability to open Telemetry Portal dashboards; blocks runbook access during incidents.
Observed: After Okta SAML/OIDC login, the identity-proxy rejects the session due to missing/altered AuthnContextClassRef (ACR) claim; session is created but RBAC denies access.
Expected: ACR claim normalization/compatibility layer should accept equivalent ACR values produced by the Okta policy migration.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Navigate to https://telemetry.redwood.internal while not authenticated.
4) Observe redirect to identity-proxy and the 403 'insufficient auth context' error page.
logs: identity-proxy (us-west) trace: authncontext_check failed: expected 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:PasswordProtectedTransport' or 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:acr:pwd', got 'urn:okta:acr:default_password' (request_id=abc123).
okta-sso audit: user jdoe@redwood.com authenticated, acr='urn:okta:acr:default_password', parental_policy='Okta-Password+MFA'.
console authz: rbac_eval denied: missing_authenticated_strength (user=jdoe@redwood.com, required=high, actual=medium).
investigation_notes: 03/10 11:05 - Triage: Pattern suggests Okta ACR string changed after a recent Okta policy rollout (internal changelog ID OKTA-2026-03A).
03/10 13:20 - Identity team confirmed an Okta ACR mapping change was deployed to dev->prod last night; mapping adds 'urn:okta:acr:*' tokens.
03/11 09:45 - Identity-proxy currently performs exact-string matching for allowed ACRs; no normalization found in code (authn/verify_authn_context.go).
03/11 10:30 - Short-term workaround tested: adding 'urn:okta:acr:default_password' to identity-proxy allowed acr list allowed affected users to access Telemetry Portal.
03/11 14:00 - Found related RBAC check requiring 'authenticated_strength: high' set by runbook gating; ACR->strength mapping not updated after Okta change.
03/12 08:15 - Cross-team meeting scheduled with Identity, Platform, and Telemetry owners to agree on canonical ACR set and mapping rules.
comments: [2026-03-10] Alex Chen: Initially reported by oncall; attaching identity-proxy and Okta traces. User unable to view critical incident graphs.
[2026-03-10] Maya Patel (SRE): Confirmed identical stacktrace across 6 incidents. Temporarily added acr token to allowlist for telemetry service in staging for validation.
[2026-03-11] Priya Kapoor (Identity): Okta team rolled the ACR change intentionally to standardize naming. We should update service-side mappings rather than special-casing Okta tokens.
[2026-03-11] Jordan Mills (Telemetry owner): Workaround worked in staging. Requesting a controlled prod rollout for allowlist change if mapping fix will take >24h.
[2026-03-12] Maya Patel: Created PR gh/infra/identity@PR-2045 to add normalization and mapping table; will coordinate canary in us-west region at 13:00 UTC.
temporary_workaround: Added 'urn:okta:acr:default_password' to identity-proxy allowed_acr list for telemetry service and updated RBAC ACR->strength mapping to treat Okta token as 'high' for the Telemetry Portal only. Documented in runbook.
root_cause: Okta ACR string format changed during a centralized Okta policy migration. Service-side authncontext matching and ACR->authentication_strength mappings required exact matches and were not updated to accept the new Okta-native token format.
resolution: In-progress: Merged normalization PR that maps Okta ACR tokens to canonical strength and trims vendor-specific prefixes. Plan: canary deploy in us-west on 2026-03-12 13:00 UTC, full prod rollout 2026-03-12 19:00 UTC after 6-hour smoke tests. Follow-up: add unit tests and an allowlist monitor alert for ACR mismatches.
next_steps: 1) Complete canary and monitor error rate / 403s for telemetry portal for next 24h.
2) Roll out normalization to other internal services (auth libraries) within 1 week.
3) Coordinate a postmortem and update Confluence runbook with mapping table.
4) Add automated alert when >1% of sessions have unmatched ACR values.
